title: Ulyana and the Smile
premise: Cyrus Ishikawa returns to the house where he grew up, now a condemned property he's been hired to survey, and finds 'Ulyana'—the smiling imaginary friend who taught him to count doors to stay safe—still waiting on the porch, unchanged after thirty years. Ulyana has been keeping the house's ledger, and the family now living there, the Okonkwos, are next on the count unless someone takes their place. As Cyrus uncovers that his own mother bargained his childhood invisibility to survive, he must choose between fleeing as he always has or offering himself to the house in the family's stead. In the end, Cyrus completes the count willingly, becoming the new thing on the porch—but he leaves the porch light on for Ulyana, who finally, gratefully, stops smiling.
about_author: K. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing vacant properties across the Rust Belt and swears three of them were occupied. They write horror about houses that remember, and live alone by choice, in a home with exactly four doors.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Cyrus arrives at 14 Marrow Lane to survey the property, keeping professional distance from a house he swore never to reenter. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; his checklist rituals hint at old survival habits.

chapters.title: Fourteen Doors
chapters.summary: Inside, Cyrus counts fourteen doors in an eight-room house. The extra doors don't open—or rather, they open inward onto rooms that shouldn't fit. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: uncanny vertigo as professional detachment begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Family Upstairs
chapters.summary: Cyrus meets the Okonkwos—Grace, her husband Tunde, and daughter Amara—who don't know the house is condemned. Amara mentions her 'porch friend.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: protective alarm; history repeating.

chapters.title: She Is Waiting
chapters.summary: At dusk, Ulyana stands on the porch exactly as Cyrus left her at age nine: same dress, same too-wide smile. She greets him by name and asks if he's finished counting yet. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror braided with guilty tenderness.

chapters.title: Rules of the Count
chapters.summary: Ulyana explains the ledger: the house counts its residents, and when the count reaches zero, it collects. His mother once paid with his visibility instead. POV: Cyrus, intercut with fragmented memory. Emotional beat: horrified understanding of his own childhood.

chapters.title: What Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Cyrus visits his estranged mother in a care facility; she recites door numbers in her sleep and begs him not to go back. She reveals she traded his childhood presence to buy time. POV: alternating Cyrus and a memory-chapter of young Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief.

chapters.title: Amara's Friend
chapters.summary: Amara has begun drawing Ulyana at school—smiling, holding out her hand. Grace dismisses it; Cyrus cannot. POV: Grace. Emotional beat: maternal denial curdling into fear as the drawings multiply overnight.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds the room behind the fourteenth door: walls papered with names, his own crossed out, the Okonkwos freshly inked. The count is nearly complete. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold clarity—he has days, not weeks.

chapters.title: Invisible Man
chapters.summary: Cyrus tries to warn the Okonkwos but his words slide off them; the house has already made him half-unreal to them, just as it did when he was a boy. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: isolation—the price of his mother's bargain, still being paid.

chapters.title: Tunde's Doubt
chapters.summary: Tunde catches Cyrus breaking in at night and, instead of calling police, admits the house hums at night and Grace sleepwalks toward the fourteenth door. POV: Tunde. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two men protecting the same family.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Story
chapters.summary: Ulyana shows Cyrus what she was: a girl the house counted first, in 1931, kept smiling on the porch ever since as its mouthpiece. She doesn't want to do this anymore. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: pity replacing fear; the monster is also a victim.

chapters.title: The First Door Opens
chapters.summary: A neighbor who once lived on Marrow Lane dies suddenly, and the ledger gains a fresh line. The house is accelerating. Grace finally sees one of the extra doors breathing. POV: Grace. Emotional beat: denial collapses; the family must run.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus uses his surveyor authority to condemn the house officially, forcing the Okonkwos out legally within 48 hours. The house retaliates: every exit door leads back to the foyer. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity against a house that cheats.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Halls
chapters.summary: Trapped inside overnight, the family endures the house rearranging itself, corridors stretching, voices imitating loved ones. Only counting aloud keeps them anchored. POV: rotating—Cyrus, Grace, Tunde, Amara. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in shared terror.

chapters.title: Amara Counts
chapters.summary: Amara, calmest of all, reveals Ulyana told her the truth weeks ago—and that Ulyana asked Amara to tell Cyrus something: 'the count can be volunteered.' POV: Amara. Emotional beat: devastating innocence; a child delivering the terrible solution.

chapters.title: Mother's Last Number
chapters.summary: Cyrus's mother dies peacefully mid-count, whispering 'fourteen.' At the funeral, Cyrus understands: her bargain ends with her death, which is why the house moved to the Okonkwos. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus tells the Okonkwos everything and gives them the deed transfer papers, then walks to the porch and offers himself to the count. Ulyana warns him what it costs: thirty years of smiling. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love against duty—duty loses, love wins.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: The house accepts. The fourteenth door opens fully; the ledger burns down to a single name. The Okonkwos flee at dawn while Cyrus holds the threshold, feeling himself become part of the architecture. POV: Grace, watching from the moving car. Emotional beat: salvation shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The New Porch
chapters.summary: Cyrus, now the house's voice, experiences time as the house does—decades like afternoons. He finds Ulyana fading, freed by his substitution, and they share one honest conversation before she dissolves. POV: Cyrus/Ulyana. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; two prisoners, one key.

chapters.title: Surveyor's Report
chapters.summary: Epilogue-style: months later, a county clerk files Cyrus Ishikawa's final report, dated but unsigned. The file notes the property 'self-maintains.' A new family views the house; the agent swears it's a bargain. POV: detached documentary voice. Emotional beat: quiet horror of the cycle continuing.

chapters.title: The Light Left On
chapters.summary: Final chapter: the house, softened by Cyrus's presence, no longer hunts—it only waits, and Cyrus keeps the porch light burning so no child ever befriends the thing on the steps again. Amara, grown, drives past once and waves. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: redemption within captivity; love persisting against the odds.

chapters.title: Counting Forward
chapters.summary: Coda: somewhere, a new imaginary friend appears beside another lonely child—but this one teaches counting as protection, not invitation, carrying Ulyana's lesson outward. The last line is a child's voice: 'One door, two doors, all mine.' POV: omniscient. Emotional beat: hope as defiance; the price of survival, paid forward.
